genZNote: Fuses infected cells together into syncytia — hence the name, and hence the bronchiolitis in infants.

habitat.hostAssociation: Obligate human pathogen, though closely related pneumoviruses infect other mammals
habitat.reservoir: Infected humans, seasonal circulation (typically fall/winter in temperate regions)

identificationClues: Causes characteristic syncytium (multinucleated giant cell) formation in infected cell culture, giving the virus its name
Rapid antigen tests and PCR of nasopharyngeal specimens are the main diagnostic methods
Leading cause of bronchiolitis and pneumonia in infants and young children
Also a significant cause of severe respiratory illness in older adults and the immunocompromised

diseases: Upper respiratory tract infection (common cold-like illness in older children/adults)
Severe lower respiratory disease in the elderly and immunocompromised
clinicalImportance.transmission: Respiratory droplets and direct contact with contaminated surfaces/secretions
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: The leading cause of hospitalization for bronchiolitis/pneumonia in infants worldwide; recently, both monoclonal antibody prophylaxis (for infants) and vaccines (for older adults and pregnant individuals to protect the newborn) have become available
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: Rapid antigen and PCR testing of nasopharyngeal specimens are the standard diagnostic approaches, largely replacing viral culture in routine clinical use

examFacts.importantTest: Rapid antigen test or PCR of nasopharyngeal swab
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: Causes characteristic syncytium formation in infected cells, the basis of its name
